title: The visual gate fails on a one-bit antialiasing flake, and a rerun deletes the evidence
foundBy: deps-maintenance pilot2 campaign, orchestrator/output/findings.md item 4, from frontend's d008 flake note

evidence.verified: At 14204bf, `npm run ci` passed with every gate run, and its `test:pixel-diff` passed 3 of 3. `npm run visual:compare` passed 5 of 5 runs on an unchanged tree, each 116/116 with 0 differing pixels. With the flake's three deltas written into both dark markdown baselines, the gate at 14204bf passes 116/116, and the gate at 7d44127 fails that tree 114/116 on 6 pixels. With lucide-react 1.47.0 installed, 14204bf fails the four captures the campaign saw fail, at 16, 64, 17 and 68 pixels, in two runs. Those runs left two directories under `visual-diff/`, and their `dark/app-shell-current.png` files are byte-identical at 93,619 bytes, beside a 93,607-byte baseline. Three measurements predate replaying these commits onto the selection-legibility work, which changed no script. Without antialiasing counted, the four lucide captures failed at the campaign's counts of 4, 16, 4 and 16. Ten captures of an unchanged tree were byte-identical to the baseline and to each other. The regression test fails at thresholds of 0, 0.003 and 0.006, and with antialiasing set aside.

resolution: The gate counts a pixel only past a pixelmatch threshold of 0.005. That is inside the measured window where the flake reads 0 and the smallest real change still counts in full. The pixel and ratio allowances stay at 0. It counts antialiased pixels too, which it used to set aside, so a change that moves only antialiasing no longer reads as zero. Each compare writes its failures to a directory of its own and deletes none, and writes each render with the browser's own bytes. A test holds the threshold from both sides.
details:
`npm run visual:compare` failed once in nine runs on trees with nothing changed. Each time it was six pixels, three on each of `dark/markdown-minimap.png` and `dark/markdown-viewer.png`. Both captures differ at the same three offsets from their bottom-right corner, (-1,-4), (-1,-3) and (-2,-2), by one least significant bit in one or two channels. It is one rounded corner whose antialiasing blend lands a bit low, in dark only. At `PIXEL_THRESHOLD = 0` any non-zero delta is counted, so the flake reads as a small real regression. The route from a red gate is a review and a re-record, which moves a frozen baseline to silence noise.

Two more defects sit on that route. `compare()` deletes `visual-diff/` before it runs, so the confirming rerun destroys the images of the run that found the difference. The campaign lost a red run's images that way. And `writeFailure` writes `<name>-current.png` as a pngjs re-encode, which is pixel-identical and about 34% larger. Copying one into `visual-baseline/` leaves an approved capture encoded unlike its siblings, which no pixel comparison notices.
